claims.title: Splitting a latent component into positive-weight observational clones preserves every finite shared-latent iid view law
claims.scope: finite latent mixture where clone emission rows are identical and clone weights sum to the original component weight
assumptions: views are conditionally iid given the persistent latent component
nonclaims: physically distinct copies with different justified measure are not being identified with bookkeeping clones

claims.title: Additive probability-weighted coarse-category mass is invariant under observational clone refinement
claims.scope: finite latent categories with component probabilities and refinement weights summing to one
assumptions: all clones retain the parent coarse-category label
nonclaims: refinement invariance alone does not uniquely determine an anthropic measure

claims.title: Uniform latent-label counting is not invariant under observationally redundant positive-weight refinement
claims.scope: finite latent labels with at least two coarse categories and equal mass assigned per represented label
assumptions: one represented label may be split into multiple positive-weight observational clones
nonclaims: the theorem concerns representational label counting, not independently justified physical multiplicity

claims.title: With one label in each of two categories, redundant refinement can drive uniform count mass for either category arbitrarily close to zero or one while preserving all finite observable laws
claims.scope: two-category finite latent mixture with repeated positive-weight clone refinements
assumptions: clone emission laws equal the refined parent emission law
nonclaims: weighted category probability remains unchanged under the same refinement

claims.title: Refining one half-mass simulated component into fifty positive-weight clones changes uniform label mass from one-half to fifty-fifty-firsts while preserving weighted mass one-half
claims.scope: the exact two-category binary-emission construction in repository tests
assumptions: equal positive split weights across the fifty clones

claims.title: Refining the opposite half-mass category into fifty clones changes the same uniform simulated-label mass to one-fifty-first without changing observations
claims.scope: the exact two-category binary-emission construction in repository tests
assumptions: equal positive split weights across the refined base-category clones
nonclaims: the example changes representation rather than physical multiplicity

claims.title: Bounded exact latent-refinement invariance audit
claims.scope: one through five shared-latent views, equal refinements up to fifty clones, unequal positive split weights, both coarse-category directions, and outcome-cap rejection
assumptions: all probabilities use exact rational arithmetic
nonclaims: bounded checks are not empirical evidence for simulation
